fields.statement: Verifier claude-code-19a95588 at b187f837: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(run-autonomy-source|describe-golden)$' -v passes both. run-autonomy-source.txtar starts a run whose workflow declares [autonomy] plan = "auto" with rhiza.autonomy.accept = owner and accept undeclared; run start, run status show '- Autonomy plan: auto from workflow declares' and '- Autonomy accept: owner from rhiza.autonomy.accept'; run status --json carries stage/mode/source/workflow; the journal's started entry carries both. describe-golden.txtar is regenerated with the new autonomy field (RunStageAutonomy) and passes. The testscript's workflow is named declares, not plan, so I also ran a real plan run by hand in a scratch root (built binary, RHIZA_ env cleared, committed .rhiza/workflows/plan.toml = builtin plan + [autonomy] plan = "auto", git config rhiza.autonomy.accept owner): rhiza run start --workflow plan --new ... --dry-run printed 'Autonomy plan: auto from workflow plan' and 'Autonomy accept: owner from rhiza.autonomy.accept'. Diff read: runAutonomy takes the workflow declaration first, else rhiza.autonomy.<stage>; Started.Autonomy is folded into State and RunInfo; runLines prints one line per stage. It records all four stages (plan, accept, ship, signoff) rather than only those the run performs, which the acceptance allows. go test ./internal/run passes, and the internal/api tests for autonomy, run start and run status pass. The full internal/api package timed out under load average ~14 on 4 cores, with TestReadBudget failing on model read timings (show/ls/ready), which this change does not touch.
